geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Practice the lessons so far, then check your answers.

Goal: I can connect circle theorems.

  • 10.1 I can identify radius, diameter, chord, secant, tangent, arc, congruent and concentric circles.
  • 10.2 I can prove the perpendicular from the center bisects a chord.
  • 10.3 I can prove a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.
  • 10.4 I can relate central angles to arc measures.
  • 10.5 I can prove an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
  • 10.6 I can prove an angle inscribed in a semicircle is right and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
  • 10.7 I can relate a circumscribed angle to its central angle.
  • 10.9 I can find angles formed by secants and tangents inside and outside a circle.
  • 10.10 I can use intersecting chord, secant, and tangent segment relationships.
  • 10.11 I can construct a triangle's circumscribed circle.
  • 10.12 I can construct a triangle's inscribed circle.
  • 10.13 I can construct medians and altitudes and locate their points of concurrence.
  • 10.14 I can explore a surprising concurrence result (the name is traditional; Napoleon's authorship is doubtful).

slides.title: Practice: 10.1
slides.html: Is every diameter a chord? Is every chord a diameter?
slides.reveal: Every diameter is a chord. A chord is a diameter only if it passes through the center.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • arc measure is arc length
  • an inscribed angle equals its arc
  • a tangent can cross the circle
  • concurrency points are always inside the triangle
